result.title: Revisiting Critic Estimation in Soft Actor-Critic Algorithms
result.summary: Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) is a widely used deep reinforcement learning algorithm that combines entropy regularization with an actor-critic architecture. Standard implementations rely on one-step temporal-difference learning of Q-functions, yet alternative critic design choices remain underexplored. In this work, we revisit three such choices: learning soft advantages instead of soft Q-values, the use of multi-step return targets, and the training of multi-step critics from replay buffer data. Keeping the policy objective fixed, we compare the six critic variants these choices generate: (i) advantage and (ii) dueling-advantage critics learned from one-step transitions, and $λ$-return and soft Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) critics learned either (iii, iv) on-policy or (v, vi) from replayed trajectory segments. Each variant is evaluated across an entire random hyperparameter search on fourteen tasks, treating the hyperparameters as part of the algorithm. Learning soft advantages instead of soft Q-values does not improve performance, and the soft GAE critic adds nothing over the simpler $λ$-return critic. What does improve performance, most clearly on continuous control, is training a $λ$-return critic on replayed trajectory segments, even without importance weighting or trace cutting. This extends earlier evidence that uncorrected multi-step targets work well under replay to the full soft $λ$-return, entropy terms included. By design, the underlying ideas studied here extend beyond SAC, and our empirical findings aim to encourage their application to a broader class of reinforcement learning algorithms.

AI.brief_summary: 该文在 SAC 中重新考察三种 critic 设计选择（soft advantage 替代 soft Q、multi-step 回报目标、从回放数据训练 multi-step critic），在 14 个任务上以整轮超参搜索比较六种变体，发现仅在回放轨迹片段上训练 λ-return critic 能稳定提升性能，且无需重要性加权或 trace cutting。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「无修正的 multi-step 目标 + 轨迹片段回放」可用于核查 LVR 中多步推理轨迹的贡献分配与监督方式，但仅在 RL 值估计中验证，向 latent 推理的迁移属推测。
